blocks.content: Work only on the webhook retry bug. Never log customer payloads.
Investigate duplicate deliveries in the synthetic webhook worker. Identify the race before proposing a patch.
Preserve the 24-hour idempotency window. A retry must reuse the original event ID; do not shorten retention when cleaning up keys.

Synthetic local trace; no production data.
$ pytest tests/test_webhook_retries.py -q
FAIL test_concurrent_retry_claims_once
worker A: received event evt_demo_17, attempt 1
worker B: received event evt_demo_17, attempt 2
worker A: cache GET seen:evt_demo_17 -> absent
worker B: cache GET seen:evt_demo_17 -> absent
worker A: enqueue job -> accepted
worker B: enqueue job -> accepted
worker A: cache SET seen:evt_demo_17 -> success
worker B: cache SET seen:evt_demo_17 -> success
Expected one queued job, observed two.
The check and write are separate operations in worker.py.
The existing sequential retry case passes; it does not cover concurrency.
A failed claim must not enqueue a second job.
Do not treat this trace as a complete test run or a measured model outcome.
The race is between GET and SET. Use an atomic claim before enqueue. Add a concurrent retry regression test.

watchlist.note: Required retention constraint; inspect the summary when this phrase disappears.
